candidates.title: [Bug]: module init returning a proper subtype of error? (e.g. DErr?, error<D>?) is rejected
candidates.body:
### Description
A module-level `init` function whose return type is a proper subtype of `error?` that contains `()` (e.g. `DErr?` with `type DErr distinct error;`, or `error<D>?`) is rejected with `'init' function must have return type '()' or 'error?'`. Aliases equal to `error?` (`type E error; ... returns E?`, `type Opt error?; ... returns Opt`) are accepted, and the same types work as ordinary return types, so only the init check is too strict.

Spec §8.4 (Function definitions): *"The following special requirements apply to the init function of a module: it must not be declared public; its return type must both be a subtype of error? and contain (); it must have no parameters."* `DErr?` and `error<D>?` satisfy both conditions. `doc/lang/subset10.md` lists function definitions without restricting `init`.

### Steps to Reproduce
```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

type DErr distinct error;

function init() returns DErr? {
    io:println("init"); // @output init
}

public function main() {
    io:println("main"); // @output main
}
```

**Actual:**
```
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: 'init' function must have return type '()' or  'error?'
 --> init-distinct-error-return-v.bal:5:1
```
**Expected:** compiles and prints `init` then `main`.

The same happens with `type D record { int code; }; function init() returns error<D>? {}`.

### Affected Version(s)
`main` @ da51086fe71a

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux, `go run ./cli/cmd run <file.bal>`

### Related area
Semantics

### Related issue(s) (optional)
#1710 (class `init` method rules; different: missing checks, not over-strict). The same over-strict check may also affect `main` (`public function main() returns DErr?` is rejected), though the spec does not state main's return-type rule.

candidates.title: [Bug]: XML children step `x/<p:e|f>` fails to parse when the first alternative is a prefixed name
candidates.body:
### Description
An XML element-children step whose name pattern has a namespace-prefixed name as the first alternative followed by `|` fails with a syntax error. Reordering (`x/<f|p:e>`), a single prefixed name (`x/<p:e>`), the descendants step (`x/**/<p:e|f>`) and the filter (`x.<p:e|f>`) all parse and work. `x/<p:e|p:e>`, `x/<p:f|e>`, `x/<p:e|p:*>` fail the same way. In other contexts (e.g. `(x/<p:e|f>).length()`) the error is `missing open paren token` / `missing close paren token`.

Spec §6.36.1: `xml-name-pattern := xml-atomic-name-pattern [| xml-atomic-name-pattern]*`, `xml-atomic-name-pattern := * | identifier | xml-namespace-prefix NoSpaceColon identifier | xml-namespace-prefix NoSpaceColon *`; §6.36.3: `xml-element-children-step := /< xml-name-pattern >`. So `p:e|f` is a valid pattern and both children of `<r>` match. subset10 lists XML navigation expressions without restriction (the `xml-qualified-names` note only applies to variable references).

### Steps to Reproduce
```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

xmlns "urn:x" as p;

public function main() {
    xml x = xml `<r><p:e>1</p:e><f>2</f></r>`;
    xml y = x/<p:e|f>;
    io:println(y.length()); // @output 2
}
```

**Actual:**
```
error[SYNTAX_ERROR]: missing identifier
 --> b1.bal:7:22
```
**Expected:** `2`

### Affected Version(s)
`main` @ da51086fe71a

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux, `go run ./cli/cmd run <file.bal>`

### Related area
Parser

### Related issue(s) (optional)
None found (checked #1293, #1589, #1132, #1633).

candidates.title: [Bug]: attribute map of a read-only xml:Element is not read-only (`is readonly` is false)
candidates.body:
### Description
`getAttributes()` on an `xml:Element & readonly` returns a map for which `is readonly` is `false`. The map is actually immutable at runtime (writing to it through a `map<string>` parameter panics with `cannot mutate readonly value`), but its read-only bit is not reported, so e.g. `readonly r = attrs is readonly ? attrs : "no";` picks `"no"`. `e.getChildren() is readonly` correctly gives `true`.

Spec §5.3.2 (XML): *"The attributes and children of an element are reachable from the element. Thus, if the read-only bit of an xml:Element is on, then the read-only bits of the mapping representing its attributes and of the xml value representing its children are also on."* lang.xml `getAttributes`: *"Returns the map representing the attributes of `elem`."*

### Steps to Reproduce
```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

public function main() {
    xml:Element & readonly e = xml `<a x="1"/>`;
    map<string> attrs = e.getAttributes();
    io:println(e is readonly); // @output true
    io:println(attrs is readonly); // @output true
}
```

**Actual:**
```
true
false
```
**Expected:**
```
true
true
```

### Affected Version(s)
`main` @ da51086fe71a

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux, `go run ./cli/cmd run <file.bal>`

### Related area
Runtime

### Related issue(s) (optional)
Related: #1698 (the opposite problem — an interpolated template is wrongly read-only).
